title: Nine at the Easiest Hole: Bletchingley Hands Mullin the Double
title_candidates: Nine at the Easiest Hole: Bletchingley Hands Mullin the Double
Baker Blinks on the 12th, Mullin Takes the Lot
The Defending Champion, the Par-3, and the Eight-Shot Gap
Four New Courses, One Man Who Behaved Himself
theme: Mullin won TEG 4 by being the only man who never had a catastrophe — four rounds above the field median, never a shot below it — while the defending champion, Jon Baker, threw the Trophy away over eight holes at Bletchingley and the rest of the field discovered that four unknown courses will happily find the worst in you.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck register: witty, affectionate ribbing, every joke anchored to a real number
opening_hook: Open on R4 H12 at Bletchingley — a 130-odd-yard par 3, stroke index 18, the easiest hole on the card — where the defending Trophy champion made nine and handed David Mullin a lead he never gave back; then loop back to Ashdown and the three days that got them there.
foreshadow: R1 at Ashdown: Mullin posts the best gross round in the field on a course with no bunkers — the Green Jacket race is effectively over before anyone notices it started
Jon Baker arrives as defending Trophy champion (TEG 3) and leads after R1 — the frame for the fall
Henry Meller arrives as reigning Wooden Spoon holder with back-to-back Spoons, and promptly makes a 12 on the par-3 11th at Ashdown
The short holes keep doing the damage: Meller's 12 at Ashdown's par-3 11th (SI 3), Baker's 9 at Bletchingley's par-3 12th (SI 18)

competitions.name: Trophy (Net VP)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (+9, by 8 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Baker led after R1 by 3; Mullin took it at Lingfield in R2 and stretched to 16 after his Crowborough +17 gross. Baker's R3 counterpunch (-3) and an outright takeover at R4 H2 made it a real fight again — and then between holes 9 and 16 at Bletchingley Baker bled 27 shots, including a 9 at the par-3 12th and an 11 at the 15th. Mullin retook the outright lead at H12 and posted the best round in the field (+1) to finish. Attribution is 'inherited': Baker outscored Mullin in two of four rounds and still lost by 8 — but Mullin was the man standing there to take it, with no round below the field median all tournament.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (+81, by 19 from Stuart Neumann)
competitions.how: Built, not inherited, and effectively over by R1: Mullin led on gross from Ashdown's 11th and was never headed, outscoring Neumann in all four rounds and posting the best gross round in the field three times. The Crowborough +17 — the 2nd-best gross round in TEG history to date — turned a 7-shot cushion into 16, and R4 pushed it to 19. Neumann's consolation: a personal-best gross total of +100, and the same for Baker (+113), Meller (+107) and Williams (+152) — the whole field improved and Mullin still won by 19.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams (+40 net VP), lost by 5 to Henry Meller
competitions.how: Williams was below the field median in all four rounds and never above it — but he was still third after R2. The bottom slot changed hands 15 times, mostly between Meller, Neumann and Williams, before Bletchingley settled it: Williams dropped to the bottom at H6 after a 9, briefly handed it back when Meller made 10 at the 11th, then took it for good at H13 and bled 16 shots over the closing six for a personal-worst +15 (+43 gross). Meller escaped his third straight Spoon by 5 — and had he simply played his own average in his worst round, Williams would have finished ahead of him.

headline_candidates: No Bunkers, No Mercy: Ashdown Finds Meller a 12 Anyway
The Reigning Spoon Holder Opens With Twelve on a Par 3
Baker Leads, Mullin Quietly Starts Tailoring the Jacket
rounds.chosen_headline: No Bunkers, No Mercy: Ashdown Finds Meller a 12 Anyway
rounds.angle: A new course for TEG, and one with no sand at all — which did not stop Meller taking 12 at the par-3 11th (SI 3), the worst hole relative to par of the whole tournament, or Williams shedding 22 over the closing nine. Baker leads the Trophy by 3; Mullin's best-in-field gross round is the day's quietly decisive fact.

headline_candidates: Lingfield's Trees and Water Take the Champion's Money
Baker Posts His Worst Round to Date; Mullin Takes the Lead
Nine at the 17th, and the Trophy Changes Hands
rounds.chosen_headline: Baker Posts His Worst Round to Date; Mullin Takes the Lead
rounds.angle: Baker bleeds 15 over holes 5-11 and adds a 9 at the 17th for a personal-worst +9; Mullin's steady +4 is enough to take the Trophy lead by 2 and push the Jacket cushion to 7. Meller's +2 — 12 better than R1 — is the round of his TEG so far and briefly makes him look like a man escaping his own history.

headline_candidates: Mullin's +17 at Crowborough: Second Best in TEG History
MacKenzie's Beacon Bows to Mullin; Williams Loses Eighteen in Six
rounds.chosen_headline: Mullin's +17 at Crowborough: Second Best in TEG History
rounds.angle: On MacKenzie's high heathland Mullin goes round in +17 gross — the 2nd-best gross round TEG has recorded — with nine straight holes (9-17) without dropping a net shot, and the lead balloons to 16 in both competitions. Baker's -3 was the day's best net counterpunch and nobody noticed. Williams lost 18 shots in the first six holes; Meller followed his good day with +13.

headline_candidates: Nine at the Easiest Hole on the Course
Baker Eagles the 8th, Then Loses 27 Shots in Eight Holes
rounds.chosen_headline: Baker Eagles the 8th, Then Loses 27 Shots in Eight Holes
rounds.angle: Baker takes the outright Trophy lead at H2 and eagles the par-4 8th — the only eagle of the tournament — and then loses 27 shots between the 9th and the 16th, including a 9 at the par-3 12th (SI 18, the easiest hole on the course) and an 11 at the 15th. Mullin retakes the outright lead at H12 with the best round in the field (+1) and completes the double; behind them Meller makes two 10s and Williams closes with a personal-worst +15 to collect the Spoon.

players.arc: Two prior Jacket wins become three and a second Trophy: never below the field median in any round, spread of just 6, best gross round in the field three times out of four — he didn't so much seize TEG 4 as stand still while everyone else fell over.

Defending Trophy champion who led after R1, led again at R4 H2, and then made 9 and 11 in the space of four holes at Bletchingley — dethroned by his own scorecard, with a personal-best gross total (+113) as the cruellest possible consolation.

Below the field median in all four rounds and still only third after R2, he saved his worst for last — a personal-worst +15 (+43 gross) at Bletchingley, 16 shots shed over the closing six — to take a first Wooden Spoon, in the same tournament as his personal-best gross total of +152.

Reigning Spoon holder with back-to-back Spoons, opened with a 12 at a par 3 and looked doomed — then posted a personal-best gross total (+107) and escaped by 5, largely because Williams was even worse over the final nine at Bletchingley.

Green Jacket runner-up with a personal-best gross total of +100, beaten in all four rounds by the same man; briefly the bottom of the Spoon race in R2 and R3 before the field's genuine strugglers reclaimed it.

venue_notes: TEG's first visit to East Sussex (and its Surrey borders), and — unusually — four courses none of which TEG had ever played: Royal Ashdown Forest's Old Course, famously without a single bunker and high above sea level, where the field found trouble anyway; Lingfield Park's mature parkland trees and water, which drowned Baker's R2; Crowborough Beacon, MacKenzie-touched heathland with South Downs views, where Mullin posted his +17; and Bletchingley, a modern, fast-draining parkland where the fast conditions produced the fastest collapses. Weave the 'no bunkers' line into R1 and the 'excellent drainage, nothing else forgiving' gag into R4.
course_history_notes: Every round of TEG 4 was a first visit for every player — no course history existed at Ashdown, Lingfield, Crowborough or Bletchingley, so nobody could blame local knowledge.
Four of the five players posted personal-best gross totals (Neumann +100, Meller +107, Baker +113, Williams +152) — and Mullin still won the Jacket by 19.
Mullin's best gross of the tournament, 88 at Crowborough (+17), stands as the 2nd-best gross round in TEG history to date.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R4 H12 at Bletchingley — Baker, outright leader since H2, makes 9 at the par-3 stroke-index-18 12th; Mullin retakes the outright lead and is never headed again.
Green Jacket: R1 H11 at Ashdown — Mullin goes clear on gross and stays there for 62 holes; the +17 at Crowborough in R3 turned a lead into a 16-shot formality.
Wooden Spoon: R4 H13 at Bletchingley — Williams drops to the bottom for the final time and bleeds 16 shots over the closing six, putting the Spoon beyond even Meller's two 10s.

payoffs.seed: Mullin's best-in-field gross round at Ashdown in R1
payoffs.payoff: He led the Jacket from R1 H11 to the last putt, beat Neumann in all four rounds and won by 19 — the race was decided before anyone had learned the course names.

payoffs.seed: Baker as defending Trophy champion, leading after R1
payoffs.payoff: He leads outright again at R4 H2, then drops 27 shots in eight holes at Bletchingley and loses by 8 — the reigning champion dethroned by the par-3 12th.

payoffs.seed: Meller as reigning Spoon holder with back-to-back Spoons, opening with a 12
payoffs.payoff: He escapes by 5 with a personal-best gross total of +107 — though had he simply played his own average in his worst round, he'd have kept the Spoon; Williams's R4 saved him.

payoffs.seed: The short holes keep doing the damage
payoffs.payoff: Meller's 12 at Ashdown's par-3 11th (SI 3) is bookended by Baker's 9 at Bletchingley's par-3 12th (SI 18) — the hardest short hole and the easiest, both fatal.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up as a supporting frame — Mullin and Baker traded the Trophy lead 20 times across four rounds — but the close-finish hard rule puts counterfactual in front, and inversion carries the defending-champion-dethroned layer that the hints only glimpsed.

why_the_champion_won: Mullin was never below the field median in any round and had the narrowest spread in the field (6 vs a median 8), so when Baker — who outscored him in two of four rounds — shed 27 shots between the 9th and 16th at Bletchingley, Mullin was the only man positioned to take it, and closed with the best round in the field.
